patterns_found.visual_evidence: The mobile sketch shows a small boxed icon with stacked horizontal lines in the top-right of the header, a conventional hamburger/menu trigger.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: Tapping the icon should open and close the site navigation. Because the desktop sketch shows visible navigation links/categories in the header area, the mobile version likely collapses those into an off-canvas panel, dropdown sheet, or expanded inline menu.
patterns_found.ambiguities: The sketch does not reveal whether the menu opens as a full-screen overlay, slide-down panel, or drawer, nor whether nested items exist.

patterns_found.visual_evidence: The presence of a hamburger-triggered hidden navigation implies a disclosure/overlay state change that must move focus appropriately when opened and returned when closed.
patterns_found.behavior_notes: When the mobile menu opens, keyboard focus should move into the revealed navigation and return to the trigger on close. If implemented as an overlay/drawer, focus containment and escape/close handling are needed.
patterns_found.ambiguities: Depends on whether the mobile menu is a simple inline expansion or a true overlay drawer.

sketch_notes: The sketches imply a mostly content-driven article page with very low JavaScript complexity. The only clear interactive behavior is responsive navigation: desktop exposes navigation directly in the header, while mobile replaces it with a hamburger toggle. The article body, share/support area, related-content cards, and footer appear as standard links/cards rather than JS widgets, and there is no visual evidence of tabs, accordions, forms, modals, sticky behavior, or progressive loading.
